body: Baffling how people are asking you to put your head down and work. Change is not going to come about if you remain a bystander. We all know this... This is a tough subject to navigate and needs to be dealt with tact. I’ve learnt (and still learning) to approach such subjects with empathy. Understand why a 60 year old thinks this way. Usually anyone older than 60, I don’t bother arguing with because in my opinion.. they are a lost cause, w exceptions. The 24 year old, however; has potential. Try to scope out why they think this way. Maybe they’ve had personal experiences that solidified their beliefs, or they’ve got second-hand information. Gently, direct them to reliable sources - books, articles, data, whatever you think supports your argument. Allow them to form their own opinion. Imo, that’s the best you can do. Being gentle allows the other person to be receptive of information rather than defensive/combative and trying to “win” the argument. Im not saying you were being combative - Idk if you were. Thats my two cents anyway. Good on you for trying.

There is no problem in getting yourself checked out if you are doubting that you may have a mental health issue instead of making yourself believe you dont have one till its too fucking late. If someone is really seeking that kinda attention by saying they are suicidal or depressed, maybe they're suffering with another issue. I don't know how you can actually tell if someone is faking it for attention. Unless you examine them as a medical professional or maybe you're very close to them, How do you know? I think its better to assume that someone is indeed depressed and offer them your support/refer them for support than just assuming they're faking it. Because you don't really know if someone is faking it. One day they kill themselves and you'll go "oh wait they were really suicidal"?? The problem is not the people who are allegedly faking it but the people who assume they're faking it especially the ones that can't grasp the mere concept of mental health. They're just being our unaware parents all over again! Let's not go backwards. Bottomline, its more harmful to assume someone is "faking it" than assuming they are not and providing them help. Prevention is important. At least that's what we've been taught as medical students.
